title: Acute pharyngitis and tonsillitis (sore throat)
subject: ophthalmology-ent
summary: Most sore throats are viral and settle within a week. Use Centor or FeverPAIN to decide who to test or treat, confirm group A streptococcus by rapid test or culture where available, and treat it with penicillin V or amoxicillin for 10 days (IDSA). Refer quinsy, airway compromise or sepsis the same day.

sections.title: Assess
items: Viral features make group A streptococcus (GAS) unlikely: cough, rhinorrhoea, hoarseness, oral ulcers. GAS causes up to 30% of sore throats in children and up to 15% in adults (IDSA 2025).
Centor (1 point each): tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes or lymphadenitis, history of fever above 38 °C, absence of cough. Score 3 or 4: 32 to 56% chance of isolating streptococcus.

FeverPAIN (1 point each): fever in the past 24 hours, purulence on tonsils, attends within 3 days of onset, severely inflamed tonsils, no cough or coryza. Score 4 or 5: 62 to 65% chance; 0 or 1: 13 to 18%.

Red flags: stridor, drooling, muffled voice, cannot swallow saliva, trismus, unilateral peritonsillar bulge with uvular deviation (quinsy), neck swelling or torticollis (parapharyngeal or retropharyngeal abscess), or sepsis.

Consider infectious mononucleosis (posterior nodes, splenomegaly, marked fatigue), scarlet fever (sandpaper rash, strawberry tongue), acute HIV, and gonococcal pharyngitis when the sexual history fits.

sections.title: Who to test (IDSA)
items: IDSA 2025 suggests a clinical score to decide who to test: a low score means testing is unlikely to help. Test high-risk patients even with a low score: household GAS contact, past rheumatic fever, or suspected complicated GAS infection (abscess, scarlet fever, toxic shock).
Confirm GAS with a rapid antigen detection test (RADT) or throat culture before treating where testing is available (IDSA 2012).
Children and adolescents: back up a negative RADT with throat culture. Adults: back-up culture is not routinely needed. A positive RADT needs no culture.
Do not test children under 3 years routinely (rheumatic fever is rare at this age) unless there are risk factors such as an infected older sibling; scoring systems do not apply under 3 years.
Do not test for cure after treatment if symptoms have resolved, and do not test or treat asymptomatic household contacts routinely.

sections.title: Antibiotics for GAS pharyngitis
items: IDSA: penicillin V or amoxicillin for 10 days. Penicillin V: children 250 mg two or three times daily; adolescents and adults 250 mg four times daily or 500 mg twice daily.
Amoxicillin: 50 mg/kg once daily (max 1 g) or 25 mg/kg twice daily (max 500 mg per dose) for 10 days.
Poor adherence or unable to take oral medicine: benzathine penicillin G as a single IM dose, 600 000 units under 27 kg or 1 200 000 units at 27 kg and over.

Non-anaphylactic penicillin allergy: cefalexin 20 mg/kg twice daily (max 500 mg per dose) for 10 days. Anaphylactic allergy: clindamycin 7 mg/kg three times daily (max 300 mg per dose) for 10 days, or azithromycin 12 mg/kg once daily (max 500 mg) for 5 days where macrolide resistance is low.

NICE (UK, no testing): FeverPAIN 0 or 1 or Centor 0 to 2, no antibiotic; FeverPAIN 2 or 3, no antibiotic or a back-up prescription; FeverPAIN 4 or 5 or Centor 3 or 4, immediate or back-up antibiotic; systemically very unwell or high risk, immediate antibiotic.

NICE adult regimen differs: phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg four times daily or 1 g twice daily for 5 to 10 days (5 days may relieve symptoms; 10 days improves eradication); clarithromycin for 5 days in penicillin allergy.

sections.title: Symptom relief
items: Paracetamol or ibuprofen for pain and fever, with adequate fluids. Avoid aspirin in children (Reye syndrome).
Medicated lozenges (local anaesthetic, NSAID or antiseptic) may reduce pain slightly in adults.
Corticosteroids are not recommended routinely (IDSA; not recommended by NICE).
Viral sore throat: no antibiotic; explain that symptoms usually last about a week and when to return.

sections.title: Refer the same day
items: Quinsy, parapharyngeal or retropharyngeal abscess, or Lemierre syndrome (sore throat followed by neck vein thrombophlebitis and septic emboli): same-day ENT for drainage and IV antibiotics.
Airway threat (stridor, drooling, tripod posture): do not force a throat examination; call senior anaesthesia and ENT.
Unable to swallow fluids, dehydrated, or signs of sepsis: admit.
Suspected diphtheria (grey adherent membrane, bull neck, incomplete immunisation): isolate, take throat swabs, give antitoxin urgently and notify public health.

sections.title: Special situations
items: India and other settings where rheumatic heart disease is common: preventing acute rheumatic fever matters more, so complete the full 10-day penicillin or amoxicillin course, or give single-dose IM benzathine penicillin, rather than a 5-day course.
Pregnancy: penicillin V or amoxicillin are safe; if a macrolide is needed, NICE prefers erythromycin.

Repeated positive tests may reflect chronic GAS carriage with viral infections; carriers generally need no antibiotics. Tonsillectomy solely to reduce the frequency of GAS pharyngitis is not recommended (IDSA).
Suspected infectious mononucleosis: avoid amoxicillin or ampicillin, which commonly cause a rash.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Prescribing antibiotics for sore throat with clear viral features.
Missing epiglottitis, quinsy or deep neck space infection behind a 'sore throat'.
Stopping penicillin after a few days of improvement where rheumatic fever prevention is the aim.
Treating asymptomatic contacts or carriers.

drugs.name: Penicillin V (phenoxymethylpenicillin)
drugs.dose: Children: 250 mg orally two or three times daily; adolescents and adults: 250 mg four times daily or 500 mg twice daily; for 10 days
drugs.notes: IDSA first line. NICE adults: 500 mg four times daily or 1 g twice daily for 5 to 10 days.

drugs.name: Amoxicillin
drugs.dose: 50 mg/kg orally once daily (max 1 g), or 25 mg/kg twice daily (max 500 mg per dose), for 10 days
drugs.notes: IDSA first line; once-daily dosing helps adherence. Avoid if mononucleosis is likely.

drugs.name: Benzathine penicillin G
drugs.dose: Single IM dose: 600 000 units under 27 kg; 1 200 000 units at 27 kg and over
drugs.notes: When adherence to a 10-day oral course is doubtful.

drugs.name: Cefalexin
drugs.dose: 20 mg/kg orally twice daily (max 500 mg per dose) for 10 days

drugs.name: Clindamycin
drugs.dose: 7 mg/kg orally three times daily (max 300 mg per dose) for 10 days

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.dose: 12 mg/kg orally once daily (max 500 mg) for 5 days
drugs.notes: Penicillin allergy; GAS macrolide resistance varies by region.

drugs.name: Clarithromycin
drugs.dose: 7.5 mg/kg orally twice daily (max 250 mg per dose) for 10 days
drugs.notes: IDSA alternative in penicillin allergy; NICE uses a 5-day course.
